_comment: Store registry — the declared source of truth for every mc_* browser-storage
key this app uses, and whether it syncs (mc-sync.js STORES) and/or is included
Why this file exists (audit G-01/G-02, roadmap K-1.1): sync coverage, export
coverage and the code's actual key usage were three hand-maintained lists that
had already drifted apart. mc_custom_exercises_v1 was documented as synced and
was in neither list; mc_session_summary_v1 was synced but not exported. Nothing
in CI could see it, because no gate compared the lists to each other.
tools/check-store-coverage.js enforces this file against mc-sync.js and
mc-export.js, and fails when code uses a key that is not declared here.
Adding a store means adding it here in the same change.
sync:   false, or the mc-sync.js merge strategy name.
export: true when the key belongs in a downloaded backup.
A key can be export-only: backing up costs nothing, syncing needs a merge rule.

mc_active_prog.note: Which program is running. Owner-classified as training data (K-1.3), so it follows the user.

mc_bio_cred.note: Biometric unlock credential. NEVER synced or exported — a secret must not leave the device that holds it.

mc_bio_optout.note: Biometric opt-out flag. Pairs with mc_bio_cred; device-scoped security choice.

mc_vitals_v1.note: Manual daily wellness entry (restingHr/sleepHrs/readiness) — flagship-immersive-roadmap.md H3. Not consumed by mc-readiness.js's per-muscle formula; see that phase's own note.

mc_coach_report_v1.note: Cached AI coach report. Derived from workout_logs, regenerated server-side.

mc_cond_src_prog.note: Conditioning entry-point breadcrumb for this tab.

mc_custom_exercises_v1.note: User-created exercises. G-01: its own module header always claimed this synced; it did not.

mc_device_id.note: Identifies THIS device to the sync layer. Syncing it would defeat its purpose.

mc_deload_v1.note: Roadmap Phase 4 step 3: the athlete accepted a lighter session in the pre-session brief. Read by mc-setlog.js's planFor(), which builds one working set fewer. Tab-scoped and timestamped on purpose — a decision about today's session, not a setting, so it is neither synced nor backed up.

mc_discard_snapshot_v1.note: Undo buffer for a discarded session. Deliberately short-lived and device-local.

mc_errors_v1.note: S6: capped ring buffer (last 20) of window 'error'/'unhandledrejection' events, written by the generated head-boot script on every page. Local debug breadcrumbs, not user data — deliberately not synced or backed up.

mc_reports_seen_v1.note: field-feedback-roadmap.md FB4: ids of this account's reports whose one-time Fixed note this device already showed (last 100).

mc_reports_outbox_v1.note: field-feedback-roadmap.md FB1: Report a problem rows waiting to reach client_reports (offline or signed out). Sent and removed by MC_REPORT.flush(); capped at 20.

mc_errors_sent_v1.note: Flagship readiness E: which mc_errors_v1 entries were already sent to client_errors, and when the last send was tried (10-minute spacing). Device-local bookkeeping.

mc_foodapi_cache_v1.note: Food-lookup API response cache. Derived data, re-fetchable.

mc_hints_seen_v1.note: K-3.4/G-11: one-time contextual coach-mark dismissal flags, keyed by hint id. Meaningless on another device — each shows itself again there if never marked seen, which is the correct fallback, not a bug.

mc_launched.note: PWA cold-launch guard for this tab.

mc_offline_prefetch_v1.note: Which programs have been crawled+prefetched for offline, and when. Pure cache bookkeeping — regenerable from the network, meaningless on another device, and would make the export file balloon with URL lists no restore needs.

mc_onboarded.note: First-run onboarding flag. Same reasoning as mc_tour_done_v1.

mc_personal_theme_v1.note: Custom theme values. Device preference, same rule as mc_theme_mode.

mc_pm_active.note: PM-mode unlock for this tab. sessionStorage by design.

mc_pm_overrides.note: Owner-only PM working copy; the published truth lives in Supabase.

mc_pm_pending_exercises.note: PM publish queue; drains to Supabase.

mc_prefs_v1.note: Rest-timer haptics / sound / cue preferences. Device preference.

mc_program_progress_v1.note: Which day of a program you are on, which days are done, and that program's rest pattern / per-week day order. Training data (K-1.3) — mid-block progress must follow you to a second device. Keyed by program id and merged per key, exactly as mc_weekly_overrides_v1 is, so advancing one program on the phone and another on the tablet does not clobber either. Day identity cannot be derived from mc_workout_log_v1 on a multi-day SPA page (see the module header).

mc_published_programs_v1.note: Cache of Supabase-published programs. Server is authoritative.

mc_replacements.note: Base name of the per-page swap keys; see the mc_replacements| prefix.

mc_push_asked_v1.note: Roadmap Phase 4 step 5: this app has had its one turn at asking for notification permission. Per-device on purpose — the permission it guards is a property of this browser, so syncing or restoring it would silence the ask on a device that never made the choice.

mc_push_key_v1.note: The VAPID public key this device's push subscription was made with. A subscription is bound to its key, so after a key rotation mc-push.js's migrate() replaces it. Per-device: it describes this browser's subscription, not the account.

mc_resume_toast_shown.note: VOC-C2: dedup guard (keyed by mc_activity.last.ts) so the "Session saved" toast fires once per departure, not once per re-render. Tab-scoped bookkeeping, not user data.

mc_session_summary_v1.note: Per-session summary. Was synced but not exported — the G-02 drift this registry exists to prevent.

mc_session_v1.note: In-flight workout session state. Resuming a half-finished session on another device is a separate feature, not a backup concern.

mc_setlog_pending_v1.note: Typed-but-unchecked set values for the open session. Same in-flight reasoning as mc_session_v1.

mc_storage_persist_asked.note: L6: one-time flag so navigator.storage.persist() is requested at most once ever, on the first completed workout.

mc_sync_reloaded.note: One-shot reload guard for this tab.

mc_theme_mode.note: Appearance. Owner-classified device preference (K-1.3): a phone and a tablet may reasonably differ.

mc_tour_done_v1.note: Quick Tour completion flag. Device preference — re-seeing the tour once on a new device is minor.

mc_setlog_deleted_v1.note: { 'storeKey|day|setNumber': {ts} }, one record per unticked set, pruned after 120 days. mc-sync.js's mergeSetlog() drops a set whose tick time is not newer than its record, so an untick on one device is not put back by the other device's copy. The backup import unions it and merges with it the same way.

mc_workout_log_deleted_v1.note: Flagship readiness R1 / D-24: { workoutKey: {ts} }, one record per workout the athlete deleted. Unioned across devices; mc-sync.js's mergeWorkoutLog() and the backup import both drop every keyed entry, so a delete on one device holds everywhere. A separate store rather than tombstones inside the log, so none of the log's twenty readers had to change.

mc_workout_log_v1.note: Every write goes through mc-log-read.js (appendWorkout / deleteWorkouts / clearWorkouts / writeWorkoutLog); tools/check-workout-log-writers.js fails CI on any other (flagship readiness R1 / D-38). mc-finish.js is the main caller.

mc_workout_archive_v1.note: Finished workouts past the log's newest 200, in a compact form (flagship readiness R7 / D-39). The log used to drop them, here and in the cloud copy. Written only by mc-log-read.js (archiveWorkouts / capLog / deleteWorkouts); synced untrimmed.

mc_backup_last_v1.note: When this device last saved a backup file, and when the backup reminder was last dismissed (flagship readiness R7 / D-36). Device state: a backup made on one phone says nothing about another.

mc_builder_draft_v1.note: The half-built custom workout (name, program, collection, exercises), so leaving the builder or closing the app does not lose it (flagship readiness R5 step 6). Cleared when the workout is created.

mc_ui_dash_v1.note: The dashboard tab and per-tab scroll this browsing session was on, so Back from a workout returns there (R5 step 6). A fresh launch opens on Home.

mc_ui_landing_v1.note: Each program landing's tab, open group and scroll position this browsing session, restored on Back or reload so a workout's Back button returns to the same place in the list (flagship readiness R6). A fresh visit opens on Overview.

mc_ui_history_tab_v1.note: History's Sessions/Programs tab for this browsing session (R5 step 6).

mc_ui_stats_mode_v1.note: The Stats body map's Recovery/Volume toggle for this browsing session (R5 step 6). H1's locked default, Recovery, still applies to a fresh launch.

mc_ex_order_today_v1.note: Today-only exercise order per workout container, stamped with the local day (flagship readiness R5 step 4). A kept order goes to mc_ex_order instead.

mc_session_adjust_v1.note: Today's + Add set / Skip exercise per exercise, stamped with the day key; anything from another day reads as empty (flagship readiness R5 step 3). The sets themselves are in mc_setlog_v1.

mc_swaps_today_v1.note: Today-only exercise swaps, per page, stamped with the local day; anything from another day reads as empty (flagship readiness R5 / D-10). A kept swap goes to mc_replacements|<pageId> instead. Not synced: a swap for today's busy machine belongs to this gym visit.

mc_workout_logs_outbox_v1.note: Per-set cloud writes (workout_logs upserts and deletes) made with no signal, replayed when the network returns (flagship readiness R3 / D-19). Device-local by nature: it holds this device's undelivered writes, and the set itself is already in mc_setlog_v1.

mc_replacements|.note: Per-page exercise swaps. Dynamic key per page id, so only matchable by prefix.

mc_streak_push_.note: Per-streak push dedup marker. Device-scoped bookkeeping, meaningless on another device.

mc_client_assign_dismissed|.note: Per-client dismissal of an assignment banner. UI dismissal state.
